message.reasoning_content: Record description update analyzing the kernel. Key risks: INT32 overflow in intermediate transforms, exactness of Winograd integer transform algebra, division by 576 (must be exact division if algebra correct; floor division with negative non-divisible would be wrong — but if exact, fine), int8→int32 loads use mask with tile*36 indexing — fine. validate_inputs uses value.is_neg? Actually torch.Tensor has no is_neg... but that's problem's own function. Also transform correctness: output transform divides by 24 per axis... 24*24=576. Check Winograd F(4,3): standard B^T uses division by 6,4, etc. Data transform has no denominators; filter transform denominators moved to output; the standard A^T has /6,/4 etc. Output transform coefficients 6,4,4,... 4(m1+m2+m3+m4)... plausible. Key risk: whether the integer identity holds exactly — needs symbolic or runtime verification. Also intermediate magnitudes: values up to ~127*9=1143 fine in int32; int64 products fine.
